titleEn: The Song of the Cid — Minaya fetches Ximena and the daughters from Cardeña (tirada 83, first part, lines 1385–1452)
part: Tirada 83 (first part) · Minaya fetches Ximena and the daughters from Cardeña (lines 1385–1452)

sentences.t:
Iffantes de Carrión [so consejo preso ane],
dando ivan conpaña a Minaya Álbar Fáñez:
sentences.l:
Infantes of Carrión [their counsel taken have],
giving they-were-going company to Minaya Álbar Fáñez:
sentences.i: The Infantes of Carrión had taken their counsel, and rode along keeping company with Minaya Álvar Fáñez:
sentences.n: Tirada 83 (assonance á) — Minaya goes to Cardeña for doña Ximena; more Castilians offer to go to Valencia; Minaya in Burgos promises the moneylenders good payment of the Çid's debt; Minaya returns to Cardeña and sets out with Ximena (the rest of Pidal's rubric — Pedro Vermúdez setting out from Valencia, Avengalvón joining him at Molina, the meeting at Medinaceli — belongs to the second half of this long tirada, part 83b). The line-ends carry a stressed á (están, assomar, rogar, mal, está, rictad …), and á-e endings (Fáñez, fagades, iffantes, alegre, mande, partes, faze, caen) count with them, their unstressed last syllable disregarded. The whole second half of v. 1385, so consejo preso ane, is in italics in Pidal's print: his restoration; the next line he numbers 1385b, keeping the traditional count undisturbed. Pidal's note to v. 1385: ane for an (= han, 'have'): 'damos una muestra de e paragógica en estos versos', 'we give a sample of paragogic e in these verses' — an extra -e sounded after a final consonant at the line-end, which he prints in italics (here in brackets) through v. 1390: Bivar[e], far[e], perdera[ve], pesar[e]. so consejo preso ane, 'they have taken their counsel' (so = su; preso, past participle of prender, 'to take'): the Infantes have made up their minds, presumably about the match they spoke of at vv. 1372–77. dando ivan conpaña, ir + gerund, 'were going along giving company', escorting Minaya as he leaves the court; conpaña = compañía.

sentences.t:
“En todo sodes pro, en esto assi lo fagades:
saludadnos a mio Çid el de Bivar[e],
somos en so pro quanto lo podemos far[e];
el Çid que bien nos quiera nada non perdera[ve].”
sentences.l:
“In all you-are profit, in this so it may-you-do:
greet-for-us to my Çid him of Bivar[e],
we-are in his profit as-much-as it we-can do[e];
the Çid who well us may-love nothing not will-lose[ve].”
sentences.i: “You are of good service in all things; be so in this too: greet my Çid of Vivar for us; we are on his side in all that we can do; if the Çid will be our friend, he will lose nothing by it.”
sentences.n: sodes = sois; pro, 'profit, good', here as an adjective, 'serviceable, worthy'. fagades, present subjunctive 2nd pl. of fazer (= hacer, f- for h-), a polite command, 'so may you do'. saludadnos, imperative + nos, 'greet him for us'. el de Bivar, 'he of Vivar'. Pidal's note to v. 1388: ser en pro de uno, like andar en pro de uno (vv. 1913, 2054), is 'tratar del provecho de uno, serle favorable y amigo', 'to look to someone's advantage, be favourable and friendly to him'. so = su; far, short form of fazer. el Çid que bien nos quiera: a relative with the subjunctive, 'the Çid, should he wish us well', the subject set first. Pidal's note to v. 1389: perderave for perderá, with paragogic e after the archaic usage; the ballads would say perderáe. The whole ending -ve is Pidal's (in italics). nada non, double negative. The Infantes' courtesy is not idle: they have just been thinking of the Çid's daughters.

sentences.t:
Respuso Minaya: “esto non me a por qué pesar[e].”
Ido es Minaya, tórnansse los iffantes.
sentences.l:
Answered Minaya: “this not to-me has for why to-grieve[e].”
Gone is Minaya, turn-back-themselves the infantes.
sentences.i: Minaya answered: “There is no reason this should displease me.” Minaya is gone; the Infantes turn back.
sentences.n: Respuso = respondió, the old strong preterite of responder. esto non me a por qué pesar[e], 'there is no reason why this should grieve me': a = ha, aver used impersonally, 'there is'; por qué, 'reason, cause'; pesar, 'to weigh on, displease' — a courteous answer that commits him to nothing. pesar[e] is the last of Pidal's sample of paragogic e's. Ido es, ser + participle of a verb of motion, 'has gone'. tórnansse = tórnanse, 'they turn back': perfect and present side by side, the usual epic tense-mixing.

sentences.t:
Adeliñó pora San Pero, o las dueñas están,
tan grand fue el gozo quandol vieron assomar.
sentences.l:
He-headed for San Pero, where the ladies are,
so great was the joy when-him they-saw appear.
sentences.i: He made straight for San Pedro, where the ladies are; and great was the joy when they saw him come into sight.
sentences.n: Adeliñó, 'headed straight' (adeliñar, v. 1309). pora = para. San Pero = San Pedro de Cardeña, the monastery near Burgos where the Çid left Ximena and his daughters in the abbot's keeping (vv. 246–56). o = donde. quandol = quando le, 'when (they saw) him', le squeezed onto quando. assomar = asomar, 'to come into view'. tan grand fue el gozo, 'so great was the joy', an exclamation with no que-clause to follow.

sentences.t:
Deçido es Minaya, a ssan Pero va rogar,
quando acabó la oraçión, a las dueñas se [fo] torn[ar].
sentences.l:
Dismounted is Minaya, to saint Peter he-goes to-pray,
when he-finished the prayer, to the ladies himself he-[went] to-turn.
sentences.i: Minaya has dismounted and goes to pray to Saint Peter; when he had finished his prayer, he turned to the ladies.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 1394: Deçido, 'descendido', 'come down' from the horse (also diçiendo del cavallo, vv. 1756, 1842). The traveller, on reaching his journey's end, first goes into the church of the place to pray before attending to his business; so again at vv. 2928–29. a ssan Pero va rogar, 'goes to pray to Saint Peter', the monastery's patron (ir + bare infinitive; ssan, the s doubled after a vowel, a spelling only). se [fo] torn[ar]: se fo = se fue, ir + infinitive again, 'he went to turn' = he turned; fo and the ending -ar are Pidal's (in italics).

sentences.t:
“Omillom, doña Ximena, Dios vos curie de mal,
assi ffaga a vuestras fijas, amas [a dos las iffantes].
sentences.l:
“I-humble-myself, doña Ximena, God you may-guard from harm,
so may-he-do to your daughters, both [two the infantas].
sentences.i: “I bow before you, doña Ximena; God keep you from harm, and do the same for your daughters, both the young ladies.
sentences.n: Omillom = omíllome (= me humillo), 'I humble myself, I bow', the pronoun squeezed to -m. Pidal's note to v. 1396: Omillom was the usual formula of reverent greeting (compare vv. 1748, 3036); likewise Dios vos curie de mal was the habitual greeting in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries (the Auto de los Reyes Magos, the Alexandre), and the poem repeats it at v. 2890. curie, present subjunctive of curiar, 'to guard'. Pidal's note to v. 1397: assi faga, a 'vicarious' verb standing in for the one before it, 'también curie', 'may He guard (them) too', as in the ballad Helo, helo por do viene: 'Alá te guarde, señora… Así haga a vos, señor'. ffaga, the f doubled, a spelling. amas a dos, 'both together' (= ambas a dos); the whole of a dos las iffantes is Pidal's restoration (in italics). iffantes, 'young people of rank', used here of the daughters.

sentences.t:
Salúdavos mio Çid allá onde elle está;
sano lo dexé e con tan grand rictad.
sentences.l:
Greets-you my Çid there where he is;
well him I-left and with so great wealth.
sentences.i: My Çid sends you greeting from where he is; I left him in good health, and with great riches.
sentences.n: Salúdavos = salúda vos, 'greets you'. onde = donde. elle = él, an older, fuller form. sano, 'in good health'. rictad, 'riqueza', 'wealth' (Pidal, v. 688). tan grand, 'so great', an intensive with no que to follow.

sentences.t:
El rey por su merçed sueltas me vos ha,
por levaros a Valençia que avemos por heredad.
sentences.l:
The king by his grace released to-me you has,
for to-take-you to Valençia which we-hold as inheritance.
sentences.i: The king of his grace has released you into my keeping, to take you to Valencia, which we hold now as our own.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 1400: sueltas me vos ha (compare v. 1408), 'os ha dejado libres', 'has let you go free'; me, 'to me', into Minaya's charge. ha sueltas: aver + past participle, the participle agreeing with the object (vos, the ladies). por su merçed, 'of his favour'. levaros = llevaros, levar. avemos por heredad, 'we hold as our heritage', as land of our own by right (avemos = hemos, aver 'to have, hold').

sentences.t:
Si vos viesse el Çid sanas e sin mal,
todo serié alegre, que non avrié ningún pesar.”
Dixo doña Ximena: “el Criador lo mande!”
sentences.l:
If you should-see the Çid sound and without harm,
all he-would-be glad, for not he-would-have any sorrow.”
Said doña Ximena: “the Creator it may-ordain!”
sentences.i: If the Çid could see you safe and well, he would be all gladness and would have no sorrow left.” Doña Ximena said: “May the Creator will it so!”
sentences.n: viesse, imperfect subjunctive of veer (= viera); serié, avrié, conditionals with the -ié endings (= sería, habría). todo serié alegre, 'he would be all glad', todo used adverbially (it could also be 'all would be glad', with todo the subject). que, 'for'. ningún pesar with non, a double negative. el Criador lo mande, 'may the Creator ordain it', mande present subjunctive of wish.

sentences.t:
Dio tres cavalleros Minaya Álbar Fáñez,
enviólos a mio Çid, a Valençia do está:
sentences.l:
Gave three knights Minaya Álbar Fáñez,
sent-them to my Çid, to Valençia where he-is:
sentences.i: Minaya Álvar Fáñez dispatched three knights and sent them to my Çid, to Valencia where he is:
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 1405: dió, 'despachó, envió', 'dispatched, sent', as at v. 1159. enviólos = envió los. do = donde. The message follows without a verb of saying.

sentences.t:
“Dezid al Canpeador —que Dios le curie de mal—
que su mugier e sus fijas el rey sueltas me las ha,
mientra que f[ó]remos por sus tierras conducho nos mandó dar.
sentences.l:
“Tell to-the Canpeador —that God him may-guard from harm—
that his wife and his daughters the king released to-me them has,
while that we-shall-be through his lands provisions to-us he-ordered to-give.
sentences.i: “Tell the Campeador — God keep him from harm — that the king has released his wife and daughters into my care, and has ordered us to be given provisions while we are in his lands.
sentences.n: Dezid = decid, imperative 2nd pl. of dezir. Canpeador, spelled with n here, as printed. su mugier e sus fijas … sueltas me las ha: the object named first and taken up again by las (compare v. 1400). mugier = mujer. mientra que, 'while'. f[ó]remos = fuéremos, future subjunctive 1st pl. of ser, 'while we shall be'; the ó is Pidal's (in italics). conducho, 'provisions' (v. 68): the king's promise of v. 1356. mandó, preterite after the perfect ha: the tense-mixing again.

sentences.t:
De aquestos quinze días, si Dios nos curiare de mal,
sermos [i] yo e su mugier e sus fijas que él a
y todas las dueñas con ellas quantas buenas ellas han.”
sentences.l:
Of these fifteen days, if God us shall-guard from harm,
we-shall-be [there] I and his wife and his daughters that he has
and all the ladies with them as-many good-ones as they have.”
sentences.i: Fifteen days from now, if God keeps us from harm, we shall be there, I and his wife and the daughters he has, and with them all the ladies, every good one they have.”
sentences.n: De aquestos quinze días, most likely 'within these fifteen days', i.e. fifteen days from now (de marking the time limit; the sense is not certain, and Pidal gives no note); aquestos = estos. curiare, future subjunctive of curiar in an open condition. sermos, 'we shall be' (= seremos): a rare shortened form beside seremos, its exact formation uncertain; [i], 'there' (Latin ibi), is Pidal's restoration (in italics); he gives no note on the line. sermos yo e su mugier …: a 1st plural verb over a list of subjects with the speaker in it. que él a, 'whom he has' (a = ha). quantas buenas ellas han, 'as many good (ones) as they have', read as all the ladies of their household; whether buenas means 'of rank' or simply 'good', and so how many are meant, is uncertain.

sentences.t:
Idos son los cavalleros e dello penssarán,
remaneçió en San Pero Minaya Álbar Fáñez.
sentences.l:
Gone are the knights and of-it they-will-think,
remained in San Pero Minaya Álbar Fáñez.
sentences.i: The knights are gone, and they will see to their errand; Minaya Álvar Fáñez stayed behind at San Pedro.
sentences.n: Idos son, 'have gone' (ser + participle, v. 1391). Pidal's note to v. 1413: e dello pensarán, 'y cuidarán de ello', 'and they will take care of it', that is, of carrying out what they were ordered (compare v. 3251). dello = de ello; pensar de, 'to see to'. remaneçió, preterite of remaneçer, 'to remain'.

sentences.t:
Veriedes cavalleros venir de todas partes,
irse quiere[n] a Valençia a mio Çid el de Bivar.
Que les toviesse pro rogavan a Álvar Fáñez;
diziendo Minaya: “esto feré de veluntad.”
sentences.l:
You-would-see knights come from all parts,
go-themselves want[n] to Valençia to my Çid him of Bivar.
That to-them he-might-hold profit they-were-begging to Álvar Fáñez;
saying Minaya: “this I-will-do of will.”
sentences.i: You would have seen knights coming from every side, wanting to go to Valencia, to my Çid of Vivar. They begged Álvar Fáñez to stand by them, and Minaya said: “This I will do gladly.”
sentences.n: Veriedes = veríais, 'you would have seen', the minstrel turning to his audience. irse quiere[n], 'they want to go off'; the n is Pidal's. Que les toviesse pro, 'that he should be of use to them', stand for them (tener pro; toviesse = tuviese, imperfect subjunctive): the que-clause set before its verb rogavan. Álvar, with v, as printed here. diziendo Minaya, a bare gerund standing for a finite verb, 'Minaya saying' = and Minaya said. feré = haré, future of fer (fazer). de veluntad = de voluntad, 'willingly' (v. 226).

sentences.i: Sixty-five knights have come to swell his following, and he had with him the hundred he had brought from there; a fine company is forming to ride with these ladies.
sentences.n: acreçídol han = acreçido le han, 'they have increased him', added to his numbers: le squeezed onto the participle, set before its auxiliary. él se tenié, 'he had with him', se an ethical dative; tenié = tenía. aduxiera, pluperfect of aduzir, 'to bring' (= había traído): the -ra form keeps its old indicative sense. d'allá, 'from there', from Valencia: the hundred men the Çid gave him (v. 1284). se faze, 'is made, is forming'.

sentences.t:
Los quinientos marcos dió Minaya al abbat;
de los otros quinientos dezir vos he que faze:
sentences.l:
The five-hundred marks gave Minaya to-the abbot;
of the other five-hundred to-say to-you I-have what he-does:
sentences.i: Minaya gave the five hundred marks to the abbot; of the other five hundred I will tell you what he does:
sentences.n: Los quinientos marcos, 'the five hundred marks' already spoken of: the Çid sent a thousand marks of silver to San Pedro, five hundred of them for the abbot don Sancho (vv. 1285–86). abbat = abad. dezir vos he = vos diré, 'I will tell you': the split future, infinitive + he with the pronoun between; the minstrel speaks to his hearers. faze = hace.

sentences.t:
Minaya a doña Xim[e]na e a sus fijas que ha,
e a las otras dueñas que las sirven delant,
el bueno de Minaya pensólas de adobar
de los mejores guarnimientos que en Burgos pudo fallar,
palafrés e mulas, que non parescan mal.
sentences.l:
Minaya to doña Xim[e]na and to her daughters that she-has,
and to the other ladies who them serve before,
the good-one of Minaya thought-them of to-equip
of the best garments that in Burgos he-could find,
palfreys and mules, that not they-may-look bad.
sentences.i: Doña Ximena and the daughters she has, and the other ladies who wait upon them: the good Minaya set about fitting them out with the finest attire he could find in Burgos, and with palfreys and mules, so that they should make no poor show.
sentences.n: The sentence starts with Minaya and his objects, breaks off, and starts again with el bueno de Minaya: a broken construction natural to oral style. Xim[e]na, the e Pidal's (in italics). que las sirven delant, 'who serve them, attend them' (delant = delante, 'before them'). el bueno de Minaya, 'the good Minaya', article + adjective + de + name. pensólas de adobar, 'set about equipping them': pensar de + infinitive, with las (the ladies) squeezed onto the verb; adobar, 'to equip, fit out'. Pidal's note to v. 1427: guarnimientos, 'vestidos y aderezo de una persona', 'a person's clothes and finery'. fallar = hallar (f- for h-). palafrés, 'palfreys', the ladies' riding horses. que non parescan mal, 'so that they may not look poor'; parescan, present subjunctive of parescer (= parecer). The buying is done in Burgos, where Pidal's rubric places Minaya and the meeting that follows.

sentences.i: When he has these ladies fitted out, the good Minaya makes ready to ride; and here are Raquel and Vidas, falling at his feet:
sentences.n: estas dueñas adobadas las ha: the object first, then taken up by las; aver + participle agreeing with it. pienssa de cavalgar, 'sets about riding' (pensar de + infinitive, v. 10). afevos, 'behold', the minstrel's pointing word (afé + vos, v. 262). Raquel and Vidas are the Burgos moneylenders who advanced the Çid six hundred marks on two chests filled with sand (vv. 85–212); Pidal's rubric calls them 'los judíos', the Jews. pie[de]s = pies, the de Pidal's (in italics): the older two-syllable form, from Latin pedes. le caen, 'they fall to him', at his feet.

sentences.i: “Mercy, Minaya, worthy knight! The Çid has ruined us, be sure of it, unless he helps us. We would forgo the interest, if he would only pay us back the capital.”
sentences.n: Merçed, 'mercy!', a plea for grace. de prestar, 'of worth' (v. 671). Desfechos nos ha, 'he has undone us' (desfazer = deshacer), the participle agreeing with nos. sabet = sabed, 'know it'. si no nos val, 'unless he helps us': val = vale (valer, 'to help'), its final -e dropped. Pidal's note to v. 1434: 'perdonaríamos los intereses con tal que nos devolviese el capital', 'we would forgive the interest provided he gave us back the capital'. soltariemos, conditional 1st pl. of soltar, 'to let go, remit'. ganançia, 'gain': the interest. que nos diesse, 'provided he gave us'; cabdal = caudal, 'capital' (Latin capitalis).

sentences.t:
—“Yo lo veré con el Çid, si Dios me lieva allá.
Por lo que avedes fecho buen cosiment y avrá.”
sentences.l:
—“I it will-see with the Çid, if God me carries there.
For what you-have done good recompense there will-be.”
sentences.i: “I will take it up with the Çid, if God brings me there. For what you have done there will be a good reward.”
sentences.n: lo veré con el Çid, 'I will see to it with the Çid'. lieva = lleva, present of levar with the stem diphthong. avedes fecho = habéis hecho (f- for h-). Pidal's note to v. 1436: cosiment, 'merced, favor', 'grace, favour'; buen cosiment y avrá, 'habrá buen pago', 'there will be good payment'; y avrá, 'there will be' (y = allí; aver impersonal). Pidal adds that in spite of this noble promise the poet never remembers the Jews again.

sentences.t:
Dixo Raquel e Vidas: “el Criador lo mande!
Si non, dexaremos Burgos, ir lo hemos buscar.”
sentences.l:
Said Raquel and Vidas: “the Creator it may-ordain!
If not, we-shall-leave Burgos, go it we-have to-seek.”
sentences.i: Raquel and Vidas said: “May the Creator so ordain! If not, we shall leave Burgos and go and look for him.”
sentences.n: Dixo, singular verb for the pair, who act and speak as one. el Criador lo mande, the words Ximena used at v. 1404. ir lo hemos buscar = lo iremos a buscar: the split future, the pronoun between infinitive and hemos, with ir + bare infinitive. lo most naturally 'him', the Çid in Valencia (it could be 'it', their money).

sentences.t:
Ido es pora San Pero Minaya Álbar Fáñez,
muchas yentes se le acogen, penssó de cavalgar,
grand duelo es al partir del abbat:
sentences.l:
Gone is to San Pero Minaya Álbar Fáñez,
many peoples themselves to-him gather, he-thought of to-ride,
great grief is at-the parting of-the abbot:
sentences.i: Minaya Álvar Fáñez has gone back to San Pedro; many men gather to him; he made ready to ride, and there was great grief at parting from the abbot:
sentences.n: Ido es pora San Pero: back from Burgos to the monastery (Pidal's rubric: Minaya vuelve a Cardeña y parte con Jimena). yentes = gentes, 'people, men'. se le acogen, 'they join him, come in under him' (acogerse). penssó de cavalgar, a preterite among presents: the tense-mixing. al partir del abbat, 'at the parting from the abbot' (partir de, 'to part from'); it could also be read 'at the abbot's leave-taking'.

sentences.t:
“¡Sí vos vala el Criador, Minaya Albar Fáñez!
por mi al Campeador las manos le besad
aqueste monesterio no lo quiera olbidar;
todos los dias del sieglo en levarlo adelant
el Çid [Campeador] siempre valdrá más.”
sentences.l:
“So you may-help the Creator, Minaya Albar Fáñez!
for me to-the Campeador the hands to-him kiss
this monastery not it may-he-wish to-forget;
all the days of-the world in carrying-it forward
the Çid [Campeador] always will-be-worth more.”
sentences.i: “So may the Creator help you, Minaya Álvar Fáñez! Kiss the Campeador's hands for me, and let him not forget this monastery; for all the days of the world, in furthering it, the Çid Campeador will ever be the more worthy.”
sentences.n: Sí vos vala el Criador, 'so may the Creator help you': sí = así, a wish, with the present subjunctive vala (valer, 'to help'). Albar unaccented here, as printed. por mi (= por mí, unaccented in the print), 'on my behalf'. al Campeador las manos le besad, 'kiss the Campeador's hands', the person said twice, by name and by le; besad, imperative 2nd pl. aqueste monesterio no lo quiera olbidar: object first, taken up by lo; quiera, present subjunctive, 'may he not wish to forget' = let him not forget; olbidar = olvidar. Pidal gives no note on vv. 1444–46. en levarlo adelant, 'in carrying it forward', read as furthering the monastery (lo) with gifts and protection; valdrá más, 'will be worth more', will grow in honour; todos los días del sieglo, 'all the days of the world', forever (sieglo = siglo). The abbot's sense seems to be that by supporting the house the Çid will add to his own worth for ever; but whether todos los días del sieglo goes with levarlo or with valdrá, and the exact construction, are uncertain. [Campeador] is Pidal's restoration (in italics).

sentences.i: Minaya answered: “I will do it gladly.” Now they take their leave and set out to ride, with the king's officer who is to attend them on the way;
sentences.n: fer lo he = lo haré, 'I will do it', the split future again (fer = fazer); de veluntad, as at v. 1418. Yas espiden = ya se espiden, 'now they take leave'. el portero, the king's officer assigned to Minaya (v. 1380): not a doorkeeper but a bearer of the king's authority on the road. ha de, 'is to'. Pidal's note to v. 1449: aguardar, 'igual que guardar, servir y atender', the same as guardar, 'to serve and attend' (v. 2168): to look after them on the road.

sentences.i: Throughout the king's land they are given provisions in plenty. From San Pedro to Medinaceli they ride in five days; and there they are in Medinaceli, the ladies and Álvar Fáñez.
sentences.n: mucho conducho les dan, an unnamed 'they', the king's people: his order of v. 1356 carried out. fasta = hasta. Medina is Medinaceli, the farthest limit of Alfonso's kingdoms (Pidal's note to v. 1382): from there on the Çid is to look after the ladies. felos = fe los, 'behold them, here they are', the presentative fe (as in afevos) with los, the ladies and Álbar Fáñez named after the pronoun that announces them. Here this part ends; the tirada runs on in the same assonance, turning back to the knights who carried the message to Valencia (part 83b).
